page.layout: One printed page: one main text column at left, running head above it, and an empty narrow column at right with the page number above it. No notes in either margin.

main_text.p: pieno ad eum occidendum conspirasse, Balbino pro eius morte Hecatombem facienti fauisse, vel denique cum militi-bus exclamasse, ex pessimo genere ne catu-lum quidem habendum: Imo ipsi Romā-ni Pontifices, Pontianus & Anterus, sub huius Imperio martyrio coronati sunt: Quin & Origenes (referente Eusebio) hac ipsa persequutione grassante, Episcopos & Presbyteros, & denique omnes vbi-que Christianos, non ad defectionem aut coniurationem aliquam aduersus imperatorem ineundam: sed ad obedientiam tolerandam, suis orationibus Parenæticis cohortatus est; in fine no-bilis istius Operis, quod contra Celsum elaboravit, calumniis Celsi respondens, luculenter & pluribus demonstrat; Christianos homines esse Imperatoris studiosissimos, omnibusque illos offi-ciis, præcipuè autem precibus pro co-rum salute effusis prosequi consuevisse. Nec dissimiliter docet, tum ipse Origen. in Comment. in cap. 13. ad Romanos, vbi præsentem controversiam ex propositio-ne eventilat, tum etiam Minutius Fœlix eius coætaneus in Dialogo, qui inscribitur

page.notes: Page number "93" at top right sits inside a decorative mark and may be partly a stamp; read as printed. Faint marks in the right margin around the middle of the page (about "n", "Z", "c") are show-through from the other side and were left out. The left edge strip is the neighbouring page and was left out. "sunt:" ends with a colon-like mark that could be a full stop. "Romā-ni" carries a tilde over the a as printed. "tur" at the foot is the last line of the text (end of "inscribitur"), not a catchword.
